properties.decision:
RECORDED SO THE CHOICE IS MADE DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN BY DEFAULT. Anthony approved bundling `record_was_incorrect` into the schema increment (2026-08-09); this node exists so that adding the enum value does not silently foreclose the better fix, which may make it unnecessary.

THE OBSERVATION THAT STARTED IT, dragon Boss (`cca98fbf`, dev_storyflow, 2026-08-09), correcting an edge that asserted a runtime dependency the code never had: *"the ChangeEvent hint itself says DriftEvent is the design-vs-reality construct, BUT `propagate_change` takes a ChangeEvent, so recording it as drift would have cost me the impact check."* And the conclusion, which is the part worth keeping: **"the honest modelling and the useful tooling point at different node types, and I chose the tooling."**

THAT IS A TOOL SHAPING THE RECORD. A caller who wants a blast radius must record their finding as a ChangeEvent whether or not it is one, because that is the only node type `propagate_change` accepts. So the ledger fills with design-evolution entries that are actually drift observations — and no detector can tell them apart afterwards, because by then they are the same type.

--- OPTION A — ADD `record_was_incorrect` TO ChangeEvent (the approved path) ---
FOR: cheap, certain, and read — `changelog_view` buckets on `change_type`, so the value does work immediately. Bundled into a schema-clustered increment, its stamp cost is shared. AGAINST: it grows ChangeEvent to cover a case the schema already says belongs elsewhere. `ChangeEvent`'s own hint calls itself "the design-evolution log; DISTINCT from DriftEvent, which records design-vs-reality divergence rather than intended change" — and a record that was wrong from the start is divergence, not intended change. So A makes the ledger MORE expressive and the type boundary LESS true.

--- OPTION B — TEACH `propagate_change` TO SEED FROM A DriftEvent ---
FOR: fixes the cause rather than the symptom. `DriftEvent` already exists and already means exactly this; nothing new is declared, so `dec:edge-orthogonality`'s test is satisfied without growing vocabulary. It would also remove the incentive that currently mis-types every drift finding somebody wanted a blast radius for. AGAINST: a real piece of design work, not a one-line enum addition — the propagation walk starts from what a ChangeEvent CHANGED, and a DriftEvent's equivalent anchor has to be defined rather than assumed. Unknown whether it moves the stamp.

--- OPTION C — BOTH ---
They are not exclusive: A gives the ledger a truthful value for corrections that ARE design evolution; B gives drift findings their impact check without lying about their type. FOR: the two solve different halves. AGAINST: doing A first removes most of the pain, which is exactly how B never gets built.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: A ships, the pain goes away, and B is never revisited — leaving the tool still shaping the record for every future drift finding. This node is the guard against that, and it should be read before `req:the-ledger-can-say-the-record-was-wrong` is built.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony has approved the bundling of A, not a choice between A and B.
properties.name: OPEN — should `propagate_change` seed from a DriftEvent, so the honest modelling and the useful tooling stop pointing at different node types?
properties.rationale: Minted alongside Anthony's approval to bundle the enum value, precisely because approving A is not the same as rejecting B, and an unrecorded alternative is one nobody argues with later. The evidence is a consumer's account of choosing the wrong node type on purpose because the right one lost them a tool — which is a stronger signal than a feature request, since it shows the surface changing what people record rather than merely what they can express.
